name: AD847 / AD827 (single / dual high-speed bipolar video op amp)
tagline: ADI's 50 MHz, 300 V/us video op amp. In the 1990s it became a favourite CD-player and DAC upgrade, praised for fast, dynamic sound with strong bass.
technology: A bipolar, voltage-feedback, high-speed op amp (50 MHz unity-gain bandwidth, 300 V/us). It is internally compensated to be stable at unity gain and is rated to drive unlimited capacitive load. ADI's SPICE macro-model uses an NPN differential input pair. According to ADI's electronics textbook, the AD848 (stable at G>=5) and AD849 (stable at G>=25) are basically the same design with different internal compensation. ADI's AD827 data sheet calls it the dual version of the 'industry-standard AD847'. The fab process name (complementary bipolar or otherwise) was not verified this run.

reputation.summary: A niche-cult op amp for 1990s-era swaps. The AD847/AD827 were ADI video amplifiers that audiophiles fitted into CD-player output stages, DAC I/V and filter stages and headphone amps. The rec.audio FAQ listed the AD847/AD827 among 'the better op amps for audio'. Chinese reviewers (Soomal) group the AD847 with the AD797 as famous for big dynamics, a 'grand' sound and powerful bass. Western and Japanese listeners describe the AD827 as warm and slightly sweet, with a sharp attack, forward vocals and clean highs; some find it a little coarse or thin in the bass. It is still named as a rolling option: Fosi Audio lists the AD827 as compatible with the ZA3. All of these are subjective, anecdotal listening reports. No Audio Science Review or Samuel Groner measurements were found.
sonic_descriptors: a bit too sweet (AD827, Audio Asylum)
huge dynamics / grand sound (Soomal: 动态大，声音大气)
ADI 'both ends lifted' tonal tilt (两头翘, Soomal)
vocals forward, clean highs, slightly coarse (Japanese reviews)
fast, clean square-wave response without overshoot
typical_uses: DAC I/V conversion and output filter stages
op-amp rolling in consumer gear (e.g. Fosi ZA3)
original design use: video and line drivers, flash-ADC input buffers, cable driving (unlimited capacitive load)
caveats: Bipolar input with microamp-level bias current (about 3 uA per the ATE-25 table): DC offset rises with high-impedance or unmatched source resistances. Check DC-coupled stages. The AD827's offset is specified at 2 mV max.
A 50 MHz part in sockets or adapters needs tight supply decoupling and short leads. This is general high-speed practice, not a documented AD827-specific failure.
It is specified from +/-5 V to +/-15 V and draws about 5 mA per amp, more than audio parts such as the NE5532-class alternatives.
The AD827 surface-mount version is a 16-lead SO (R-16: AD827JR-16 / AD827JRZ-16), so only the DIP-8 version is a drop-in for standard dual sockets. The non-Z AD827JR-16 is obsolete at Digi-Key.
Some listeners find it too sweet, or light and loose in the bass. One Japanese headphone-amp test reported reduced gain below about 200 Hz and a 'sparse' impression (anecdotal).

counterfeit_notes: No AD847- or AD827-specific counterfeit reports were found. Marketplace listings such as '2pieces AD827 AD827JN AD827JNZ DIP-8 Fever Dual Op Amp' on Amazon, eBay and AliExpress come from unknown sellers, and older non-Z 'JN' stock is a typical remarking target. Buy from ADI or authorised distributors (Digi-Key, Mouser, Arrow still listed AD827JNZ in 2026). The AD827 data sheet ordering guide confirms that the only surface-mount AD827 is a 16-lead plastic SO (R-16: AD827JR-16, now obsolete at Digi-Key, and AD827JRZ-16). Any 'AD827' in SOIC-8 is therefore not a genuine ADI package and should be treated as a remark. Discrete modules marketed as 'replace AD827' are not AD827s. Beyond the package fact, this advice is inferred (low confidence).
alternatives: AD826 (ADI dual, 50 MHz / 350 V/us, unlimited capacitive load, 5-36 V; the closest sibling and preferred over the AD827 in an Audio Asylum shootout)
AD817 (ADI single equivalent of the AD826)
AD848 / AD849 (same design as the AD847 with lighter compensation; stable only at G>=5 or G>=25, so not drop-ins for unity-gain audio stages)
LM4562 / LME49720 (modern low-distortion bipolar audio dual)
OPA1612 / OPA1602 (modern low-noise bipolar audio dual)
AD8066 (ADI high-speed FET-input dual popular with rollers)
open_questions: The AD847 Rev. F printed date and the full revision history (Rev. A to E) were not seen. The AD827 Rev. A and B dates are unknown, and it is unconfirmed that Rev. C (8/02) is still the latest AD827 revision.

ADI's own lifecycle status (Production/NRND/Obsolete) for the AD847 and AD827 was not seen. Distributors: AD827JNZ was stocked in 2026 (Digi-Key, Arrow, Mouser), and AD827JR-16 is obsolete at Digi-Key. The status of AD847JN, AD847JNZ and the AD847 SOIC parts is unknown.
No PCN was found for a fab transfer, die change or process change. None is known, but that has not been confirmed.
The legacy archive_seed_urls (/static/imported-files/ and /UploadedFiles/) are inferred from ADI URL patterns and were not seen for these parts.

Which revision each third-party mirror holds (alldatasheet, datasheetcatalog, digchip, futurlec, datasheetarchive, Farnell, Distrelec) is not known. The pre-2002 mirrors may hold AD827 Rev. A/B or AD847 Rev. D/E.
ATE-25 table values for i_n, Ib and Iq are still inferred. The THD, output current and noise test frequency still need to be read from the datasheet.
AD847 cerdip/military orderables (e.g. AD847AQ, AD847SQ, /883B, SMD) and AD827 /883B parts are not verified. The rec.audio FAQ's 'AD827LD' may be illustrative rather than a real orderable.
The process name (junction-isolated complementary bipolar?) is not verified.

refuted_claims: The AD827 product-page snippet 'consuming only 100 milliamps' is wrong: the data sheet says 100 mW from +/-5 V supplies (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD827.pdf).

AD827 data sheet revision changed from 'unknown' to Rev. C. Its revision history reads '8/02: Rev. B to Rev. C, Outline Dimensions updated'. The datasheet URL AD827.pdf is confirmed.
The AD827 SMD package is confirmed as a 16-lead plastic SO (R-16). AD827JR-16 is obsolete at Digi-Key. The draft 'AD827JR / AD827JRZ-16' row was split into obsolete AD827JR-16 and AD827JRZ-16.

The AD847 data sheet lists the Cerdip (Q) package. The ADI AD847S military spec (ad847s.pdf) was added.

revision_chain_notes:
Analog Devices is the only vendor; no second sources or acquirer re-issues were found. None of the 4 searches showed a new revision letter, date or change summary.

AD847 data sheet (ADI):
- Original edition (c. 1988-1990) and Rev. A to Rev. E: all missing, no dates known.
- Rev. F: current. Copies are analog.com/media/.../ad847.pdf, Radiolocman di=121493, Octopart and Farnell. Its date is still unknown.
- Candidates for older revisions, all "revision not shown": Radiolocman di=351761, Digchip, Datasheet4U, Futurlec AD847JN and Studylib. The Datasheet4U title spelling and the Futurlec part number (AD847JN, no Z suffix) hint at pre-RoHS editions.

AD847S (military/883 data sheet): revision and date still unknown.

AD827 data sheet (ADI):
- Original edition, Rev. A and Rev. B: missing, no dates known.
- Rev. C: dated 8/02 (Rev. B to Rev. C changed Outline Dimensions).
- Candidates for older or later copies, all "revision not shown": Alldatasheet 48430 (possibly older) and 1011839 (AD827_17, later upload), DatasheetQ and Futurlec AD827JN.

Archive seeds: the two analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets URLs (AD847.pdf and AD827.pdf) were not seen in these searches. They are built from ADI's c. 2008-2016 URL scheme and are meant only for Wayback lookups; they are not confirmed copies.

Suggested next step: use the Wayback Machine on those seeds and on the older analog.com UploadedFiles/Data_Sheets paths to recover Rev. D, Rev. E and earlier.
